takeaway: In compartment syndrome, pain worsens on passive stretch of the affected muscles. Pain on passive big toe extension means flexor hallucis longus: the deep posterior compartment.

question.text: A man has had tibial nailing 3 h ago and has severe pain on passive extension of the big toe, with less pain at the ankle. What is the likely diagnosis?

answer.text: Compartment syndrome of the deep posterior compartment of the leg

lines.text: Three hours after a tibial nail, this man is in severe pain. Think compartment syndrome.
The key sign is pain on passive stretch of the muscles in the affected compartment.
Here, passively extending the big toe hurts the most. That stretches flexor hallucis longus.
Ankle dorsiflexion and plantar flexion cause much less pain.
Flexor hallucis longus sits in the deep posterior compartment, with flexor digitorum longus and tibialis posterior.
The anterior compartment holds tibialis anterior and the extensors, so it does not fit.
So the answer is the deep posterior compartment.
lines.say: So the answer is the deep posterior compartment. (clears throat)
